notes.title: Game on Sale
notes.notes:
Hey guys, once again thank you for following the game! Wanted to let everyone know the game's on sale for 50% so would be awesome if you spread the wordːsteamhappyː

Also wanted to beg the community for some more reviewsːsteamsadː

I'm greatly appreciative of Steams review system and understand the positive side of negative reviews. The players who have given my game negative reviews however don't seem to invest very much energy toward trying to understand the game from a constructive perspective. I say this because the bulk of negative reviews seem to be less than a paragraph and site very little details about the games purpose or comparison in its genre.

I'm not saying remove those reviews, just hoping someone out there understands where I'm coming from and can help me stand up against it with some positivenessːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Wanted to thank everyone for following!
notes.notes:
Really appreciate it! I follow the discussions closely and wish I could have everything done overnight. I have so many ideas for the Land Of Lamia and on top of adding some cool features to this chapter, i'm looking at ideas on how to get the next chapter funded and created with a budget to include some (next level) features. Wanted to thank you all for being patient with me as I'm still just a single person team. Also wanted to ask if you could write a review for the game?ːsteamhappyː I'm a little light on reviews and could use a boost! also, if you like the game, please share it with a friendːHecshː even one more follower means a lot to me ːsteamsadː

Cheers!

Nathan Sisler

notes.title: Puzzling Synchronised Siblings In The Land Of Lamia
notes.notes:
In case you hadn’t gathered from the weekend posts I’ve been etching into the sacred tomes of RPS lately, I’ve got a soft spot for puzzle games. The Land of Lamia [Facebook page] is one that I missed when it launched at the tail end of last month, but it’s a good ‘un. Like many of its contemporary puzzling cousins, Land of Lamia is retro-inspired – not so much in the pixelated visuals department, but more in its awkward fixed camera views and bastard hard difficulty.

notes.title: Final Release on Monday!
notes.notes:
Well, it's been a long journey creating this game. For those who haven't figured it out, I'm a single person developer. Well, not sure if I'm allowed to say that, I did everything except Sound, and Character animation because if I did those things, the game might look and sound like a robot. Big support for my sound girl Daria Kondrakhina, and character animator Mike Walters. I'm really proud of this game, proud of myself for finishing what I set out to do, proud of humans for creating these tools to build it, thankful to Steam for Green Lighting me!

However, the story is far from over. Thomas and Lily are still trapped in the land of Lamia. Will they ever make it out? who knows, I hope so..

notes.title: New feature for Level 1
notes.notes: I've gotten a lot of good feedback about the difficulty of the game and while going through components, I realized I had some large colliders on the characters for the first level. I made some big adjustments which simply softens the difficulty for the level. Level 1 still looks and feels the same just plays more fluidly. I also added a feature which emits a sound cue in level 1 when you are near danger. Other updates include: updated the animation for the opening part 2 implemented an animation from my character animator Mike Walters. Also added sound effects and music throughout the game from my sound girl Daria Kondrakhina. The game is around 98% complete and very close to final release. Still completely playable to completion, just want some players to play it through for minor bugs.

notes.title: First update
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, thanks for following The Land of Lamia. 

I've gotten some really good feedback about the game and taken the opportunity to add the following:

-Press any key to skip intro or cut scenes you've already watched. 

-Updates to sound, new music.

-Fixed annoying bugs. 

Game is still playable to completion! Only reason the game is currently on Early Access (aside from minor polish) is I'm still looking for some passionate players to attempt to finish the game and give some honest feedback about the whole experience. This game in its current state has some puzzles which really make you think, the kind of thing I really love about adventure games. I know I'm a rare breed in gaming and hope I might communicate with someone who understands what I'm going for but also the general Adventure-game demographic's taste. 

This game was inspired by some of my favorite fantasy movies from the 80's but I've come to realize this game's greatly inspired by one of the masters of this genre Lewis Carroll. So if that kind of story and riddles appeal to you, please give this game a try!
